speaker: Doctor
text:
Doctor 1: The clinical presentation is textbook for Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion (SIADH). We have severe euvolemic hyponatremia (Na 122 mEq/L), inappropriately elevated urine sodium (45 mEq/L), and inappropriately concentrated urine (Osm 334 mOsm/kg) despite low serum osmolality. Crucially, we have ruled out the major differentials: hypothyroidism (normal TSH), adrenal insufficiency (normal cortisol), hypovolemia (euvolemic status), and renal failure (normal Cr). The patient's history as a long-term smoker raises a significant red flag for a paraneoplastic syndrome, specifically Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC), which is a leading cause of SIADH.
